label: Research only. Not a recommendation to buy or sell. This desk never places trades. Stocks only, no option contracts.

keeper._note: Update keeper (features.self_heal_keeper). One keeper job sleeps until check_after_min minutes past each New York slot (weekdays, NYSE holidays skipped) and starts that slot's update only if it did not run and the last update started over min_gap_min minutes ago. After chunk_min minutes (at most 340; GitHub stops a job at 360) it starts the next keeper. Turn the switch off and the keeper stops at its next wake and does not chain. At verify_after_min past each slot it checks that the slot's run succeeded and that data/meta.json price_as_of reached that day. A failed slot gets one retry (max_tries 2 means the run plus one retry, never more); a run still going is looked at again every recheck_min minutes. Stale data after a success is recorded in the keeper run, not retried. It only triggers the normal slots and at most one retry of a failed slot, so Yahoo traffic does not grow.

light_mode._note: Light mode. features.light_mode shows or hides the Theme switch (Dark, Light, Match device) at the top of the left menu. With the switch hidden the whole desk stays dark. default_theme is what a phone or iPad sees before it picks one: dark, light, or device. The pick is saved on that device. match_device_option shows the Match device button. Colors only; nothing new is downloaded.

vcp._note: VCP scanner (vcp.html). A stock is listed only when the trend template is 8 of 8 and it has at least min_pullbacks tightening pullbacks (default 2, the green VCP tag). READY is that tag at or under the buy line. BROKEN OUT today is a close over it on at least 1.5 times the 50-day volume. WATCHING is 8 of 8 with two or more pullbacks and the close already over the buy line without that volume, or an open trade whose buy printed at 8 of 8. A name with only one pullback stays off the list. Set min_pullbacks to 1 to list those as WATCHING again. show_weaker_trend brings back stocks under 8 of 8, labeled WATCHING (trend not 8/8) and listed last, and does not use min_pullbacks. Those rows never feed Buy setups or Leaders. Nothing new is downloaded.

canslim._note: CANSLIM page (scanner_canslim.csv), strict screen (features.canslim_strict, on). A stock is listed only when it passes every rule. C: latest quarter EPS at least c_eps_min % over the year-ago quarter (required), and, only when revenue for that quarter and its year-ago quarter is on file, sales at least c_sales_min % up or growing faster than the quarter before. A: latest year EPS at least a_eps_min % over the year before (required). ROE (net income / year-end equity, only when both are on file and equity is positive) is shown against a_roe_min %; it is a pass/fail rule only when a_roe_gate is true (false by default, Nick: loosen it). Positive earnings (eps_positive_gate, true by default, Nick): the latest quarterly EPS and the latest annual EPS must both be above 0, so a shrinking loss does not count as growth; with no EPS on file the stock already fails C or A and the value says not verified. N: close within n_near_high_pct % of the 52-week closing high. S: 20-day average volume at least s_adv_min shares; accumulation, when s_accum_sessions sessions have volume, is total volume on up-close days divided by total volume on down-close days over the last s_accum_sessions sessions (unchanged days count for neither), labeled accumulation at s_accum_min_ratio or above and distribution below it; it is a pass/fail rule only when s_accum_gate is true (false by default, Nick: loosen it). BROKEN OUT today is a close above the prior 252-session closing high on volume at least s_breakout_vol_mult times the 50-day average. L: RS Rating at least l_rs_min. I (features.canslim_i_13f_trend, on): the number of distinct 13F filers holding the stock (data/inst_13f_history.csv, built by inst_history.py from the free SEC Form 13F data sets) is flat or rising from the second-newest to the newest complete quarter; a drop of i_flat_tolerance_pct % or less counts as flat; a move of more than i_max_jump_pct % either way is not verified (usually a CUSIP change, e.g. a retired CUSIP OpenFIGI no longer maps); fewer than two back-to-back complete quarters on file is not verified and does not fail. Turn canslim_i_13f_trend off for the old check (Nasdaq 13F summary shows institutions bought at least as many shares as they sold; no 13F row is not failed). features.inst_13f_history (on) lets a full run add a new quarter once the SEC publishes its next 13F ZIP (checked once a day). Light trend check: close above the 50-day and 200-day simple averages and the 50-day above the 200-day. M never blocks or demotes a stock: when SPY or QQQ closes under its 200-day EMA the page shows a market-in-correction banner (features.canslim_market_banner). READY is within ready_near_high_pct % of the 52-week closing high; WATCHING is the rest. Rows rank by rs_score inside each status: rs_score = rs_score_w6 * RS6m + rs_score_w3 * RS3m, where RS6m and RS3m are the stock's return minus SPY's return, in percentage points, over rs_6m_sessions and rs_3m_sessions sessions. Missing data stays blank and says not verified. Turn features.canslim_strict off for the old price-and-RS screen with its soft tier. Saved data only, no new download.

relative_strength._note: MarketSmith / O'Neil style RS Rating, 1 to 99, the desk's one RS score (relative_strength.py). Worked out on every run from the daily closes already saved (cache/ohlcv.csv.gz). No new download. A quarter is quarter_sessions trading days (63, about 3 months). Q1 is the latest quarter, then Q2, Q3 and Q4, each its own 63 sessions (discrete quarters, so the latest quarter really counts double). Raw score is weight_q1*Q1 + weight_q2*Q2 + weight_q3*Q3 + weight_q4*Q4. The rank is 1 to 99 across every stock on the desk with a full year of closes (min_bars, today plus 252 sessions); 99 is the strongest. ETFs and funds (the ETF column of the saved Nasdaq Trader files, the sector ETFs, SPY, QQQ) are left out and stay blank. A stock with less than a full year is blank, not 0. It is not measured against SPY. CANSLIM L, the scorecard L (pass at 80), Leaders, the RS 70 filter, the Minervini screens, Highest EPS and RS, the Chart Viewer and Nick 360 all read this number. leader_min is the RS 70 filter line. feature.rs_rank shows or hides only the RS column and the RS 70 filter; the screens still use the number. The VCP page's rule 8 (stock over SPY, the RS line) is a separate check and is unchanged.

eps_fill._note: EPS fill for the EPS Rating (feature.eps_fill). Rebuilds each company's quarterly and yearly EPS from the SEC companyfacts file the desk already downloads: more EPS tags tried period by period, periods with no SEC frame, fiscal Q4 worked out as the full year minus the 9-month year to date, net income divided by diluted shares when no EPS tag exists, and stock splits fixed from restated filings. Saved in cache/eps_history.csv on each full run. Rating rules when on: the 3 to 5 year growth span skips a loss at its start (shorter_span_on_loss), a company with a loss year still gets a yearly part ranked below every real growth rate (rank_loss_makers), and a latest quarter more than max_quarter_age quarters old counts as missing. Highest EPS and RS still needs a real multi-year growth rate. Companies the SEC has no recent quarters for (mostly foreign 20-F and 40-F filers) use the saved Yahoo earnings history (use_yahoo_saved, no new download) or a saved Nasdaq earnings-surprise history (feature.eps_fill_nasdaq): one free Nasdaq request per such name, at most nasdaq_per_run names a full run, each at most every nasdaq_refresh_days days (nasdaq_empty_retry_days when the page was empty). That page has 4 quarters, so a year-over-year change appears once a fifth quarter is saved. One company's quarters always come from one source. feature.sec_share_class_cik lets a share-class ticker missing from the SEC list (CWEN-A) use its base ticker's CIK.

marketsmith_screens._note: MarketSmith style screens: Highest EPS and RS (eps-rs.html, under Fundamental), Minervini 1-Month (minervini-1m.html) and Minervini 5-Month (minervini-5m.html, under Technical). Saved daily bars, saved SEC EDGAR EPS (cache/quarters.csv and cache/annual.csv, split-adjusted) and the RS Rating only. No new downloads and no paid data. EPS Rating is 1 to 99: the latest quarter's EPS versus a year ago, the quarter before that versus its year ago (when on file; require_prior_quarter makes it required), and yearly EPS growth over the longest span from max_years down to min_years. The three parts are ranked across the desk, averaged with equal weight, and ranked again. Highest EPS and RS lists EPS Rating at or above min_eps_rating and RS Rating at or above min_rs, best EPS plus RS first, at most max_rows. A stock more than extended_past_pivot_pct above its buy point (from VCP, Box, Flag, Qullamaggie or Marios), or with no buy point more than extended_above_sma50_pct above its 50-day, is extended and left out. Minervini 1-Month and 5-Month: price above the 50, 150 and 200-day, the 50-day above the 150 and 200, the 150-day above the 200, price at least template_above_low_pct above the 52-week low and within template_within_high_pct of the 52-week high, RS Rating at least template_rs_min, and the 200-day higher than rising_1m_sessions (1-Month) or rising_5m_sessions (5-Month) sessions ago. Each screen has its own switch: feature.scanner_eps_rs, feature.scanner_minervini_1m and feature.scanner_minervini_5m.

scanner_groups._note: Technical and Fundamental split (features.split_tech_fund). With it on, the left menu puts every screener page under a Technical or a Fundamental heading, in the order listed here, and the Chart Viewer gets a Technical | Fundamental switch (chart_viewer.group_toggle) whose list picker, All technical stocks or All fundamental stocks list, and Why box show only that side. Each key is a page id (the name in chart-viewer.html?list=...): vcp, box, flag, qullamaggie, marios, ep (Episodic pivot), gapup (Gap Up), min1m (Minervini 1-Month), min5m (Minervini 5-Month), week52 (52-week), breakouts (52-week breakouts), volume (High volume), pullbacks, breakdowns, trends, wheel, canslim, leaders, epsrs (Highest EPS and RS), growth, quality, dividend, scorecard (Stock scorecard), and top (Top stocks). The value is technical or fundamental; any other word leaves that page where it was and out of both. Buy setups and Watchlist are in both sides of the Chart Viewer. Today, Watchlist, Buy setups, Trading Floor, Paper Test, Alerts, Backtest, Options, Earnings, Sentiment, Financials, Macro, and the market pages (Gainers and losers, Breadth, Sector performance, Heatmaps, under Market) are not screeners and stay outside both. Turn features.split_tech_fund off for exactly the old menu and viewer. Nothing new is downloaded.

chart_viewer._note: Chart Viewer page (chart-viewer.html). Full-screen charts you swipe through, one stock at a time. It reads the saved daily bars and the scanner files only. No new downloads. include_trends is on, so the Trends list is in the picker on the Technical side: only Uptrend rows from the saved trends.csv, which means the price is above the 20, 50, 100, and 200-day averages. The Why box uses that label and the SMA alignment. Those stocks count in All technical stocks and in All scanner stocks. Turn include_trends off to leave the list and those counts out. features.trends still turns the Trends page itself off. Every option has its own on/off switch. chart_touch_pan is on, so a one-finger drag moves the chart back and forward through the saved history (about five years) and a pinch zooms; only a quick flick (swipe_max_ms or less, at least swipe_min_px wide) changes the chart, and a sideways swipe on the header row (ticker, price, counter) always does. The chip bar changes the chart only when every chip fits; on a phone, where it is wider than the screen, a swipe there scrolls the chips instead. drag_mode_toggle shows the Drag chip that switches between Drag: move chart and Drag: next chart on each device. range_months and range_months_phone set only the first view, which fills the width once the chart is laid out and is put back after full screen or a turn of the screen; a range you dragged to is kept when the screen turns or full screen opens or closes, until a range chip is tapped; range_chips shows 3M, 6M, 1Y, and All. fit_wide_ranges is on, so All, or any range too long to fit, fills the space left of the Why box with as much history as fits at the thinnest bar spacing (min_bar_spacing, 0.3 px) and keeps the newest candle just left of the box, like the India desk; turn it off to go back to the old view, which on an iPhone showed only a couple of bars for All. native_fullscreen_ios is off, so on an iPhone or iPad Full screen fills the page without Safari's own full screen and its grey X over the stock name; turn it on to use Safari's full screen again. Computers always use the browser's full screen. group_toggle shows the Technical | Fundamental switch at the top when features.split_tech_fund is on: the list picker, All technical stocks or All fundamental stocks, and the Why box show only that side (Buy setups and Watchlist show in both), and the last pick is saved on each device; default_group (technical or fundamental) is where a device starts. The sides come from the scanner_groups block. With group_toggle or features.split_tech_fund off the viewer is the old single one with All scanner stocks. why_box_top_left is on, so the Why box sits at the top left of the chart and the newest candle stays a small fixed gap left of the price axis on every chart; turn it off to put the box back in the lower right and leave room for it again. weekly_toggle shows Daily | Weekly. Daily is the start. Weekly bars are built in the browser from the saved daily bars (Monday to Friday: first open, highest high, lowest low, last close, volume added up, and a week that is not finished still counts). Averages are worked out on the bars on screen, so MA 10 on Weekly is 10 weeks. range_months_weekly (24) and range_months_weekly_phone (12) are the first view for Weekly, 2 years or 1 year. hide_range_chips is on, so the 3M, 6M, 1Y, and All buttons are hidden; turn it off to bring them back (range_chips can still hide them). bars_toggle shows Candles | Bars. Candles is the start. Bars are a high-to-low line with a left tick for the open and a right tick for the close. Up bars are blue (bar_up, and bar_up_light in light mode) and down bars are pink (bar_down, and bar_down_light). Each pick is saved on the device. dense_default is on, so every chart opens at the same candle width (target_bar_spacing 5.8 px, the iPad portrait daily chart): a phone, an iPad, daily, and weekly all use it, and the newest candle stays 12 px left of the price axis. min_bar_spacing_px (3) is the thinnest those candles get, and max_bar_spacing_px (8) stops a short history from stretching fat. Turn dense_default off to open on range_months / range_months_phone and the weekly month spans again. Turn the whole page off with features.chart_viewer. rs_line draws a thin RS line in the lower part of the price chart, below the candles and above the volume, on its own hidden scale so it does not move the price: the stock close divided by the SPY close, like the India desk does against the Nifty 50. SPY comes from data/index_ohlc/SPY.csv, which the desk already saves, so nothing new is downloaded. A blue dot is a new 52-week high in that line (252 daily bars, or 52 weekly bars); an amber dot means the line made that high before the price did. The RS line chip hides it on each device. Turn rs_line off to remove the line and the chip. eps_chip shows an EPS chip (EPS 85) right after the RS chip: the 1 to 99 EPS Rating from scores.csv (eps_rating, the same number as Highest EPS and RS), green at eps_chip_green_min (80) or higher, plain below, and no chip when the stock has no EPS Rating. Turn eps_chip off to remove it. comp_chip shows the Composite Rating chip (Comp NN) right after the EPS chip, green at comp_chip_green_min (80) or higher, and no chip when a stock has no rating. ms_look gives the chart a MarketSurge look: blue up bars and red down bars, bars as the first view, a white grid with no vertical lines, the 50-day average in red and the 200-day in black (10-week red and 40-week black on a weekly chart), and volume bars in the same colors; ma_21 adds a 21-day EMA chip, off by default; volume_avg_line draws the red 50-day average volume line (10-week on weekly). patterns draws the base found by base_patterns.csv on the chart with its name, depth, and length; pattern_history also draws the older bases, lighter; pattern_labels shows the name; pivot_lines draws the dashed pivot line; buy_zone shades the 5% buy zone above the pivot; pattern_caption shows a one-line summary under the chart; scanner_pivots draws the VCP, Box, and Flag pivot lines. marketsurge_style (on, needs ms_look) makes the chart look like a MarketSurge daily chart: pure white background with a faint dotted grid, thin blue up bars and magenta down bars, about a year of daily bars on the first view (ms_range_months 12, ms_range_months_phone 6, ms_right_space_pct room on the right), thin 21-day green, 50-day maroon, 150-day (10-week) tan and 200-day black lines, a thin dark blue RS line inside the price chart, thin blue and red volume bars with the red 50-day average line, each base as a light shaded box with a small name and a short dashed pivot line with its price, small rating chips, and the Why box hidden until the Why chip is tapped. rs_rating_label writes RS Rating NN at the end of the RS line. swing_labels writes small prices at swing highs and lows (swing_label_bars on each side, swing_label_min_move_pct apart). eps_markers puts a small triangle and EPS +NN% (versus the same quarter a year before) at the bottom of the price chart on each report day, from data/eps_marks.csv (eps_marks.py: SEC quarterly EPS the desk already saves, with the report day from earnings_history.csv when it has one). pivot_header adds +X% from Pivot in N days next to the price. breakout_arrows draws a small up arrow under a breakout day whose volume was at least 40% above the 50-day average (base_patterns.breakout_volume_pct). pattern_fill (off) shades the inside of each base; off, like MarketSurge, bases are thin lines only and no bar is covered. ms_shade_max_weeks (30) leaves a longer base unshaded even with pattern_fill on. ms_zone_bars (12): the buy zone is a small faint band, pivot to 5% above, over only the last that many bars and the right margin. ms_pivot_line_bars (10): the dashed pivot line covers only the last that many bars of the base plus a short stub past it. Each base is drawn in its own shape: a smooth bowl for a cup or saucer with its handle, a W for a double bottom, and a thin top and bottom line with end ticks for the others, labelled with name, depth, weeks, and Stage (for example Cup w/ Handle 23% 9w Stage 2(b)), grey and marked failed when the breakout failed. ms_hide_why starts the chart with the Why box hidden (the Why chip shows it and the pick is saved). ms_log_scale uses a log price scale, like MarketSurge, so equal percent moves look the same size. Turn marketsurge_style off to go back to the earlier look. Dark mode keeps its own colors. No side panel and nothing new is downloaded.

chart_colors._note: Moving average line colors, shared by every price chart: the Chart Viewer (chart-viewer.html) and the expand-in-place row charts on the scanner and list pages. The same color is used for the line, its toggle chip, and its value in the legend. ma_colors is for dark mode: MA 10 green, MA 20 orange, MA 50 blue, MA 150 yellow, MA 200 red. The row charts' SMA 50, SMA 150, and SMA 200 use the 50, 150, and 200 colors; their SMA 21 and EMA lines keep their own colors. ma_colors_light is used in light mode, with slightly darker shades so each line still shows on white (yellow is #ca8a04). Each value is a #RRGGBB color. A missing or bad value falls back to these defaults. Colors only; nothing new is downloaded.

episodic_pivot._note: Episodic Pivot scan. Original Qullamaggie and Stockbee rules on cached daily bars, earnings dates, and Yahoo profiles. No new downloads. Every rule has an on/off switch and its number here. Percents are whole numbers (10 means 10%). Money is US dollars. The nick_ switches are Nick's own extra filters and are off by default. The time stop only flags NO FOLLOW-THROUGH; it never closes a trade. Turn the whole page off with features.scanner_ep.

composite._note: Composite Rating, 1 to 99 (composite.py), written to scores.csv as composite_rating for the Chart Viewer chip. A close copy of the IBD idea, since IBD's formula is private. Each piece is turned into a 0 to 100 percentile across the whole desk, the pieces a stock has are blended with these weights (missing pieces are left out and the rest scaled up), and the blend is ranked across the desk again into 1 to 99. w_eps is the EPS Rating, w_rs the RS Rating, w_high how close the price is to its 52-week high, w_sales the latest quarter's sales growth versus a year ago (yearly sales growth if the quarters are missing), and w_margin the net margin over four quarters (ROE if missing). min_parts is how many pieces a stock needs, and the RS Rating is always one of them. features.composite_rating turns it off. Saved data only, nothing new is downloaded. Research only.

eps_marks._note: EPS markers for the MarketSurge-style Chart Viewer (eps_marks.py), written to data/eps_marks.csv: one row per quarter for the last quarters quarters, with the report day and the EPS change against the same quarter a year before. The EPS is the SEC quarterly EPS the desk already saves (cache/eps_history.csv), so it is reported (GAAP) EPS, not the adjusted EPS MarketSurge shows. The report day is the earnings_history.csv day within match_days of the quarter end when the desk has one, else the SEC filed day when it came within fresh_days, else the quarter end plus the stock's usual filing lag (default_lag_days when unknown). features.eps_marks turns it off. No new download. Research only.

base_patterns._note: Base pattern recognition (base_patterns.py) for the Chart Viewer, written to data/base_patterns.csv. It follows the public O'Neil and MarketSmith Pattern Recognition rules, so it will not match MarketSurge on every stock. Each pattern has its own switch: cup_handle, cup, saucer, double_bottom, flat_base, ascending_base, ipo_base, consolidation (off: it is no longer a catch-all, only a tight range of consolidation_max_depth or less over consolidation_min_weeks that fits nothing else). Every base except an IPO base needs a prior uptrend (require_prior_uptrend): the left side high prior_uptrend_pct above the lowest low of the prior_uptrend_bars before it. The left side high is a left_high_days high. Robust bounds (robust_bounds): a one-bar spike wick does not set a base's low or depth; a low more than spike_atr_mult 14-day ATRs under the lowest low of the spike_neighbors bars on each side is clipped to that line (never above the bar's close). Tight start (prefer_tight): the base starts at the true left-side high, the peak right before the correction; when the stock topped out within tight_start_pct of that price again later, each later top is tried as the start and the tightest valid base wins. An ascending base also lists its three pullback lows (pullback_low_dates) so the chart draws a rising line through them. Cup with handle and cup: cup_min_weeks to cup_max_weeks, cup_min_depth to cup_max_depth deep, or up to cup_max_depth_bear when SPY was bear_market_drawdown or more below its 1-year high at the cup's low (allow_deep_in_bear; the row says deep_base). A rounded bottom, not a V: at least cup_round_min_share of the days within cup_round_band of the way up from the low. The right side comes back cup_recover_handle of the way for a handle, or cup_recover_plain with no handle. Handle: handle_min_days to handle_max_days, handle_min_depth to handle_max_depth deep (handle_max_depth_bear in a weak market), in the upper half of the cup, holding the 10-week line (handle_above_10wk), and drifting down, not wedging up (handle_drift_down: the back half of the handle dips to within handle_wedge_tol % of the front half's low or lower). Saucer: a cup of saucer_min_weeks or more and saucer_max_depth or less deep. Double bottom: double_min_weeks to double_max_weeks, double_min_depth to double_max_depth (double_max_depth_bear in a weak market), second low undercutting the first by double_max_undercut or less. Flat base: flat_min_weeks to flat_max_weeks, flat_max_depth or less. No base (flat, IPO, or any other) is shallower than min_depth: a pinned price is a pending deal. Ascending base: asc_min_weeks to asc_max_weeks, three pullbacks of asc_min_pullback to asc_max_pullback with higher lows, the whole base asc_max_depth deep or less, each rally topping the one before (within asc_high_tolerance %). IPO base: ipo_min_weeks to ipo_max_weeks, up to ipo_max_depth, only with ipo_max_history_days of history or fewer. Base count (count_stages): bases since the last major low, counted over count_lookback_bars; a base whose low undercuts the prior base's low starts again at Stage 1, and a base only counts as a new stage when the stock first rose stage_new_pct above the prior pivot, else it is 2(b), 2(c). The pivot is the handle high (cup with handle), the middle peak (double bottom), or the base high (the rest). The breakout is the first close above the pivot; breakout_volume_ok is yes when that day's volume is breakout_volume_pct or more above the 50-day average. A base is FAILED (mark_failed) when price closes failed_pct or more below the pivot within failed_window_bars of the breakout, before it gained failed_unless_gain_pct. A live breakout older than completed_after_bars is COMPLETED. The buy point is the pivot plus buy_point_cents, and the buy zone runs buy_zone_pct above the pivot. Bases shown end in the last lookback_bars; max_per_stock keeps the newest. features.base_patterns turns it off. Saved prices only, nothing new is downloaded. Research only.

gap_up._note: Gap Up scanner (gap-up.html). A true gap: the open is above the previous day's high (true_gap_only off measures from the previous close instead). Gap % is open divided by the previous high, minus 1; the gap over the previous close is shown too. min_gap_filter on keeps only gaps of at least min_gap_pct, a whole percent (3.0 means 3%); off, any size of true gap counts. Gap-day volume must be at least vol_mult times the average of the vol_avg_days sessions before the gap day. The last close must be at least min_price dollars, and the average daily traded value (close times volume) over the last liquidity_days sessions at least min_dollar_volume, the same $3 million 50-day floor the Episodic Pivot scan uses. Hold rule: no close since the gap day below the gap day's low; a close equal to the low still holds. Gap days come from the last lookback_days trading days, today included, and the newest holding gap is the row. skip_stale leaves out a stock whose last bar is older than SPY's. Gap Up does not feed Buy setups. Every rule has an on/off switch. Cached daily bars only. No new downloads. Turn the whole page off with features.scanner_gap_up.

qullamaggie._note: Qullamaggie breakout scan on cached daily bars. Every rule has an on/off switch and its numbers here. Percents are whole numbers (3.5 means 3.5%). Prices and money are in US dollars. Marios uses these for the shared rules unless the marios block sets its own.

marios._note: Marios breakout scan. Shared entry rules come from the qullamaggie block. Keys here are Marios's own and win over the qullamaggie block.

trading_floor_paper._note: Paper test of the Trading Floor's BUY calls with FAKE MONEY (paper-test.html, features.trading_floor_paper). It starts with start_cash fake dollars on the first full run (Nov 3, 2026) and only goes forward; nothing is replayed. Each BUY call on a full run waits for the next session and is bought at that session's open, on the next full run, from the saved daily bar. A call is skipped when the stock is already held or waiting (skip_if_held), when max_open positions are open or waiting, or when free fake cash is under one position. Each position is position_pct percent of start_cash, in fractional shares rounded to share_decimals (fractional_shares off buys whole shares). With skip_gap_past_plan on, a stock that opens at or under its stop or at or over target 1 is not bought. Stop and target 1 are frozen at the call. Every daily bar from the entry day on: an open at or under the stop sells at the open; an open at or over the target sells at the open; a day that touches both counts as the stop; else the stop or target price; after time_stop_days trading days (the entry day is day 1) it sells at the close. The state is in data/paper_trades.csv, data/paper_equity.csv, and data/paper_summary.csv. Only the full run changes them, and running the same day twice changes nothing. No real orders, no broker, no alerts, no new downloads. Rules: docs/trading_floor_paper_rules.md.

trading_floor._note: Trading Floor page (trading-floor.html, features.trading_floor). Six desk roles debate today's top picks: the Buy setups list in its own order, then (fill_from_scanners) stocks READY or BROKEN OUT today on at least fill_min_scanners pattern scanners, max_stocks in all. News, Scout, Charts, Skeptic, and Sentiment each give +1, 0, or -1 and the Chief adds them: Charts veto (no valid entry, stop, and target) is SKIP; a total of verdict.buy_min_total or more with no Skeptic hard no is BUY; verdict.wait_min_total or more is WAIT; under that is SKIP. News uses the desk's stored headlines first; only picks with none get one free Google News RSS request each, on the full run, once a day (news.google_news), cached in cache/trading_floor_news.csv. Percents are whole numbers (5.0 means 5%). Volume ratios compare today with the 50 sessions before it, like the High volume page. Every check has its own on/off switch. Research only: no orders, no broker, no alerts. Rules in plain words: docs/trading_floor_rules.md.

liquid_names._note: Other common stocks (features.liquid_names and indexes.liquid). On the full run the desk reads the Nasdaq stock screener (one download that includes last sale and volume), keeps US-listed common stocks with market cap above min_market_cap dollars, last sale above min_price, and screener volume above min_volume that the Nasdaq Trader symbol files call a common stock, and adds the ones that are not already on an index until the scored list reaches max_stocks. ETFs, funds, warrants, and preferreds are skipped. The screener volume is the session volume the feed reports, not a 30-day average, because that field is not in the free screener and this step does not add Yahoo calls. No Yahoo request. Off leaves the S&P lists, the Nasdaq-100, and the growth names as they are.

slow_sources._note: Yahoo profiles and Nasdaq 13F/insider on a full run. Each name is its own request, so the whole daily list no longer fits in the job. One run refreshes at most batch_per_run names: any still missing, then the ones last refreshed longest ago. A name already refreshed inside refresh_every_days waits. Hourly runs still reuse the cache and make no extra calls.

sec_facts._note: A full run fills company facts for the whole universe (full_universe). It prefers the official nightly companyfacts.zip (use_bulk_zip) and falls back to one request per company at under 8/sec. The older daily slice (batch_per_run, refresh_every_days, features.sec_rolling) is used only when full_universe is off. cik_overrides replaces a ticker that the SEC ticker file points at the wrong filer. XOM is Exxon Mobil Corporation, CIK 0000034088. HONA, SPCX, and VYLR already point at the companies that own those tickers; they have no 10-K yet, so yearly rows stay blank.

earnings_calendar._note: Nasdaq earnings calendar on a full run. One request per weekday for the next days_ahead calendar days, starting from today so the window crosses into January by itself when the year changes. A failed fetch keeps the saved calendar. Next earnings is filled only where it is still missing.

incremental_prices._note: Daily prices (features.incremental_prices). On: each run asks Yahoo only for the days since the last saved bar, starting overlap_days calendar days earlier, and merges those bars into cache/ohlcv.csv.gz. Older bars stay, so a short download cannot wipe a stock. The newest bar is not part of the adjustment check, because it is still forming during the day. An older overlap close that moved by more than the wider of adjust_tolerance_dollars and adjust_tolerance_pct percent of the old close (0.05 means 0.05 percent, not 5 percent) is treated as a split or dividend adjustment, and that one symbol is downloaded again for history_period. repair (on) does that full download once for a symbol with fewer than repair_below_bars saved bars, such as a history cut down to a single day, and does not repeat it if the full download is still short. refresh (on) redownloads adjusted history on the after-close run only. refresh_mode weekly does everyone when the last full refresh is at least refresh_every_days old. refresh_mode slice does one of refresh_slices slices each after-close run. The first full run after this is turned on starts the weekly clock and does not redownload five years that day. chart_concurrency is how many chart calls run at once (1 or 2). The same backoff as the rest of the desk still applies. backfill_per_run (40) is how many brand-new names a regular 10:15 or 18:30 run downloads in full. features.fast_history_backfill (on) is the one-time catch-up: stock_desk.py --backfill, and the Fill new price history workflow, download fast_backfill_per_run (600) names that have no saved bars, two chart calls at a time, and may chain up to fast_backfill_max_runs (4) runs. That path does not fetch profiles, filings, news, or options, and it does not raise the cap on the regular runs. Turn the switch off after the new names have history. Off: every run downloads history_period for every symbol with the old parallel download and replaces the price file.
